source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A previous ACE-inhibitor cough makes losartan contraindicated even when there was no angioedema.","B":"Losartan is expected to cause cough at approximately the same frequency as lisinopril in this situation.","C":"Losartan prevents cough completely, so any cough after the switch must have a nonmedication cause.","D":"Cough can still occur, but it was less frequent with losartan than lisinopril in trials of patients who previously had ACE-inhibitor cough."}}
source_row.rationale: DailyMed losartan labeling reports controlled trials in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough in which cough occurred less frequently with losartan than with lisinopril. A prior cough alone is not equivalent to a contraindication to an ARB.
source_row.source_detail: Adverse Reactions — Cough: controlled trials in patients with prior ACE-inhibitor cough compare losartan with lisinopril. source_row.stem: A client stopped lisinopril because of a persistent ACE-inhibitor cough and is starting losartan. Which teaching about cough is most accurate?
